[[File:CovertShroudManeuver-TLC1.jpg|thumb|right|250px|[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] using a Covert Shroud Maneuver to lure the [[Chimaera/Legends|''Chimaera'']].]]
{{Quote|You don't have a shroud. You make one.|[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] before [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] creates a shroud by destroying a TIE fighter|<ref name="Allegiance (novel)">[[Allegiance (novel)|''Allegiance'']]</ref>}}
The '''Covert Shroud Maneuver''' was an escape tactic developed by [[Starship/Legends|starship]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] to avoid being caught in a [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]]. The maneuver called for the fleeing starship to eject a cloud of reflective particles that actually reflected the beam in various directions, allowing the starship to break free of the beam and escape. This resulted in a loop snarl in the tractor beam system, which shut the targeting system down completely.

A variant of the maneuver was a last-ditch escape or infiltration plan. It employed a smaller ship hidden inside a larger one, obscuring the true mission of the smaller vessel. When the larger ship became caught by a tractor beam, the crew set the larger ship to auto-destruct, creating a cluster of reflective pieces that confused the tractor beam targeting system. This allowed the crew to escape in the smaller ship. This maneuver was popular during the reign of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] because it was virtually impossible to counteract.

[[File:720_Shroud.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The covert shroud gambit, as employed by Luke Skywalker.]]

In [[9 ABY]], when [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] used the manoeuvre to escape a trap set by [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]], tractor beam operator [[Rejlii Mithel]] used an innovative, if ultimately ineffective, technique to attempt to recapture his ship. Mithel expected to be executed for his failure (having recently seen [[Cris Pieterson|another officer]] suffer a similar fate), however Thrawn was impressed by his quick thinking and instead tasked him with developing an effective countermeasure. 

The newly promoted [[Lieutenant]] Mithel determined that his solution would have been successful, had the targeting computer been able to handle the relevant sensor data and recommended that computer technicians be assigned to make the appropriate adjustments. His communique to Thrawn on the matter was intercepted by the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. 

[[19 ABY/Legends|10 years later]], when [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] attempted to use the gambit to escape the Star Destroyer ''[[Relentless]]'', he was astonished when his yacht, the [[Lady Luck/Legends|Lady Luck]] was recaptured, forcing him to surrender. The con artist [[Flim (Human)|Flim]] (masquerading as a resurrected Thrawn) informed him that they'd had plenty of time to develop a response since Skywalker's escape. 

==Behind the scenes==
This maneuver was used by [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] in ''[[The Last Command]]'' along with the fact that the destruction of the ship created reflective particles that would distract the tractor beam computers, with the targeting computers trying to lock on all of the particles at once and went into a loop snarl. This trick is also called the '''Covert Shroud Maneuver''' for some reason, being also called by this name in several other stories as well. A mistake at some point must have caused both of these tricks to be called by the same name.
